Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they cover (1) module-level A/B selection, (2) system-level candidate evaluation, and (3) an automatically generated “next fix” report to address failures/regressions.

## 1) Module autopilot (pick best module variants)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for afterward:
- A summary indicating which module variants were promoted/selected.
- Any modules marked “regressed” or “inconclusive” and why (often insufficient sample size or high variance).
- Since there are **no PASS candidates**, expect either “no change” (champion remains) or “needs more data”.

## 2) System autopilot (evaluate full-system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to check:
- Whether any system candidate beats `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` on the primary metric(s).
- Pay attention to both **mean** and **min** (your handoff shows both are tracked). If “min” is a robustness/worst-case metric, a higher min usually matters a lot.

## 3) Generate next-fix guidance (actionable to-do list)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
Then open:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

This report is typically the fastest way to move forward when there are **no PASS candidates**: it should tell you which component(s) are blocking promotion and what to adjust next.

## If any step fails / produces nothing useful
Send back:
- the console output from each command (or the last ~200 lines),
- and any newly generated report paths,
and I’ll help interpret results and decide whether to re-run with more trials, adjust thresholds, or patch a specific module.
